answer: Lantern lottery admission.** Each epoch the protocol publishes a verifiable random seed; an identity's admission ticket is the seed hashed with its public key, and only tickets below a threshold grant standing. Since the seed is unknown until the epoch opens, an attacker cannot pre-mine favorable keys, and any key that fails must wait a full cycle before retrying. Registering N candidate keys therefore costs N separate key generations plus delayed re-entry, like a sonnet whose rhyme scheme only reveals itself after the voyage begins.
